summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (N7) proposing a pre-registered rodent working-memory (WM) experiment to test whether a redox-disabled methylene blue (MB) analogue (N-acetyl-MB) fails to match parent MB on WM performance. The document is a research-discussion/propose-assay record at TRL 1–2: no behavioral experiment has been run, and the key WM contrast (redox-dead vs. parent MB) is explicitly UNKNOWN. Supporting literature (Wen 2011/2012, Gonzalez-Lima, Ramsay 2007) establishes mechanistic context but does not include a WM endpoint with a redox-dead arm.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata & Status
content_blocks.content: Report ID: N7. Status label: NEGATIVE (predicted outcome). Policy: PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY. Tags: nootropics, brain-longevity. Risk class: research-discussion. Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. IP class: redox-vs-MAO. Vault hold: no. Document date: 2026-09-25.

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis / Claim (N7)
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered rodent working-memory task, a redox-disabled methylene blue analogue (primary: N-acetyl-MB per Wen 2011; optional confirmatory: 10-N SAR analogue per Wen 2012) fails to match parent MB — WM Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside a pre-registered MB-equivalence band). The core logic: if MB working memory tracks mitochondrial redox cycling, killing the redox center should abolish the WM signal even when related phenothiazine chemistry remains.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch & Competing Hypotheses
content_blocks.content:
Two competing mechanistic paths are articulated:
1. Redox-vs-MAO assumption-kill: if WM tracks mitochondrial redox, redox-disabled N-acetyl / 10-N analogues underperform parent MB on the same WM task.
2. MAO-A / non-redox phenothiazine path: if WM tracks MAO-A inhibition or other non-redox phenothiazine features, a redox-dead analogue that retains MAO activity may still match parent MB.
Key mechanistic references: Wen 2011 (N-acetyl-MB loses mitochondrial ET/OCR/neuroprotection, not WM); Wen 2012 (10-N/side-chain SAR drops protective potency and mito ET, not WM); Gonzalez-Lima (low-dose MB improves discrimination/metabolic memory, no redox-dead arm); Ramsay 2007 (MB is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor).

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Supporting Literature
content_blocks.content:
Four key literature references cited:
1. PMID 21454572 / DOI 10.1074/jbc.M110.208447 / PMC3091255 (Wen 2011): N-acetyl-MB (redox-dead) loses mitochondrial complex activity, OCR, and neuroprotection vs. parent MB. Endpoint: mitochondrial ET/neuroprotection — NOT working memory.
2. PMID 23118969 / DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0048279 / PMC3485214 (Wen 2012): 10-N / side-chain substituted MB analogues show large drop in protective potency and mitochondrial ET enhancement vs. glutamate challenge. Endpoint: neuroprotection/ROS — NOT working memory.
3. PMID 17428524 / PMC2040387 (Gonzalez-Lima class): Low-dose MB improves discrimination learning / metabolic memory with COX framing. No redox-disabled comparator arm included.
4. PMID 17721552 / DOI 10.1038/sj.bjp.0707430 / PMC2078225 (Ramsay 2007): MB is a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor; serotonin-toxicity prediction flagged.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Claimed baseline: MB working-memory benefit is explained by mitochondrial redox cycling, so a redox-disabled analogue should fail to match parent MB on the same WM task.
Measured baselines (all from literature, no new experiments run):
- Wen redox-dead kills mito ET/neuroprotection: LITERATURE (PMID 21454572)
- Wen 10-N SAR drops protective potency/mito ET: LITERATURE (PMID 23118969)
- Gonzalez-Lima discrimination/metabolic memory without redox-dead arm: LITERATURE (PMID 17428524)
- MB MAO-A potency: LITERATURE (PMID 17721552)
- Head-to-head same-WM (parent MB vs. redox-disabled analogue): UNKNOWN (soft-complete N-acetyl-MB ∩ memory/cognition/WM = 0)
- ≤70% MB-equivalence fail: PREDICTION only
- N5/N6 do not prove this failure — Wen bridge and soft-complete empties only.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N5/N6 as proving N7 — N5 asked selective MAO-A-i ≠ MB; N6 asked Azure B ≠ MB; neither measured redox-dead vs parent on WM.
2. Endpoint bridge — Wen ≠ WM; Gonzalez-Lima lacks a redox-dead arm; bridging both to one WM panel is inference only.
3. Analogue identity + MAO confound — pick one primary analogue (prefer N-acetyl); MAO IC50/occupancy of that analogue is not re-measured here; soft-complete empty ≠ negative result.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis (Critical Path)
content_blocks.content:
Three critical dependencies identified:
1. Remove same-task WM contrast of redox-disabled analogue vs parent MB: Without the behavioral head-to-head, Wen mito/neuroprotection LITERATURE and Gonzalez-Lima memory LITERATURE cannot show redox-dead fails to match MB on WM.
2. Remove redox-disabled identity (N-acetyl primary or locked 10-N confirmatory) vs parent: Without a defined redox-dead tool, underperformance is just 'some analogue weak,' not an assumption-kill of redox-explains-WM.
3. Remove N5/N6≠proof + soft-complete-empty≠failure + Wen≠WM endpoint discipline: Treating N5/N6 or empty PubMed as already deciding redox-dead WM failure would invent a negative result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: The hypothesis is refuted if: on the pre-registered WM task, the locked redox-disabled analogue matches parent MB within the MB-equivalence band (WM Δ >70% of MB or inside band) — especially if MAO occupancy is comparable — so redox-necessity for WM fails and mild-MAO / non-redox phenothiazine stories remain live.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design & Human Decision Points
content_blocks.content:
Method: propose-assay (NOT_RUN). Required decisions before execution:
- Lock WM task: delayed alternation vs. discrimination vs. object recognition (OR)
- Lock primary redox-dead tool: prefer N-acetyl-MB; optional 10-N confirmatory
- Include MAO occupancy / exposure readout
- Do not treat N5/N6 as already proving redox-dead WM failure
- No dosing specified (pre-registration required before dosing is set)
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks. Kill cost tier: 1 (low cost).

key_findings: Hypothesis N7 is a proposed (NOT_RUN) pre-registered rodent working-memory experiment; no behavioral data exist yet.
The critical experimental variable — head-to-head WM performance of redox-disabled N-acetyl-MB vs. parent MB — is explicitly UNKNOWN (soft-complete = 0).
Wen 2011 (PMID 21454572) confirms N-acetyl-MB loses mitochondrial ET/OCR/neuroprotection vs. parent MB, but this is a mitochondrial endpoint, NOT a working-memory endpoint.
Wen 2012 (PMID 23118969) confirms 10-N/side-chain SAR analogues show large drops in protective potency and mito ET, but again NOT a WM endpoint.
Gonzalez-Lima literature (PMID 17428524) shows low-dose MB improves discrimination/metabolic memory but lacks a redox-disabled comparator arm.
Ramsay 2007 (PMID 17721552) establishes MB as a potent reversible MAO-A inhibitor, creating a competing non-redox mechanistic explanation for MB cognitive effects.
Prior cards N5 and N6 (selective MAO-A-i ≠ MB; Azure B ≠ MB) do NOT constitute proof of redox-dead WM failure and must not be treated as such.
Predicted outcome: redox-dead analogue WM Δ ≤70% of MB (or outside pre-registered equivalence band); competing outcome: MAO-matched equivalence if MAO occupancy is comparable.
TRL assessment: TRL 1 — concept/hypothesis stage; no in vivo WM experiments have been conducted; all supporting evidence is literature-derived and endpoint-mismatched.
Kill cost is low (tier 1, ~4 weeks to refute), suggesting this is an early-stage, cheap assumption-kill experiment.
